newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian house rejects move to bar private insurers.
newsitem.headline: Indian house rejects move to bar private insurers.

text.p: India's lower house of parliament on Wednesday rejected a communist-backed measure to bar private firms from the state-controlled insurance industry.
The amendment to the insurance regulatory bill, proposed by a deputy from the Communist Party of India-Marxist, lost by a 228 to 43 vote.
The bill, which would create the Insurance Regulatory Authority, was expected to be put to a final vote later in the day.
The government proposed in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to open the health insurance sector to a small number of private Indian companies.

Another amendment to the insurance regulatory bill, backed by the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party, to bar multinational companies from the insurance sector was pending when the lower house adjourned for lunch.
